clue.text: Nominal source of condiment

the dried berry that is ground to make black pepper

clue.text: Description of a scoundrel when the chip are down?

definitions.text: Description of a scoundrel when the chip are down?

parts.words: Description of a scoundrel when the chip are down?
parts.note: plays on Samuel Johnson's saying that love of country is the last refuge of a scoundrel: when all else fails he wraps himself in the flag

explanation.definitionFit: Johnson called patriotism the last refuge of a scoundrel, so in a crisis the rogue turns flag-waver.

clue.text: Good to engage in absolute clear out

indicators.note: the good letter is fitted inside the absolute word, as a gear engages

parts.note: pure means absolute, as in pure nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid or clear out, often of unwanted people.

clue.text: Court involved in vote? Shocking

parts.note: an election is a vote

explanation.definitionFit: Death or injury by electric shock: shocking taken literally as a noun.

clue.text: A grateful expression maintained by family from part of Spain

clue.text: Fail to include it with high honour

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

clue.text: Berries suitable for those feeling peckish?

definitions.text: Berries suitable for those feeling peckish?

parts.words: Berries suitable for those feeling peckish?
parts.note: peckish means wanting a peck, a kiss, not hunger: the white-berried plant under which people kiss at Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: Hanging Christmas greenery with white berries is a licence to kiss anyone standing beneath it.

clue.text: Attractive way to dive into river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river
ST is short for street, a way

clue.text: Drinks spelling the end for flirting girls

definitions.meaning: alludes to Dorothy Parker's line that men seldom make passes at girls who wear spectacles

clue.text: Unskilful writer held back in computer studies

clue.text: Absolutely false story about end of tight road race

clue.text: Term for a night one gets drunk, nothing less? No, somewhat later!

explanation.walkthrough: 'gets drunk' rearranges TERMFORANIGHTONE once 'less' has taken out an O ('nothing'). 'No' only joins the definition to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the next morning, a while after the night before, typically with a hangover.

clue.text: Leader of band heading off leader of soldiers

clue.text: Home refrigerator ultimately needs ice shifting

shifting means the letters of these words move around

clue.text: Source of charge —- assault?

clue.text: Showing pace and power in attack
